plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 15.2.7
plan.contextChunk: This figure is part of a worked example asking to evaluate the line integral of (xy + z^3) ds from (1, 0, 0) to (-1, 0, pi) along a helix. The figure shows a 3D rectangular bounding box with x ranging from -1 to 1, y from -1 to 1, and z from 0 to pi. A single helical curve C spirals inside the box from the labeled starting point (1, 0, 0) at the bottom to the endpoint (-1, 0, pi) at the top, with a directional arrow indicating the orientation of traversal. The figure shows the geometry of the helix C in xyz-space, establishing the path and its orientation for setting up the arc-length line integral using the parametric equations x = cos t, y = sin t, z = t for t in [0, pi].

elements: rectangular bounding box (12 edges): x from -1 to 1, y from -1 to 1, z from 0 to pi
x-axis label 'x' near front-bottom-right with tick marks at 1, 0, -1
y-axis label 'y' near top-right with tick marks at 1 and -1
z-axis label 'z' on the left vertical edge with tick marks at 0 (bottom) and pi (top)
blue helical curve C: x=cos t, y=sin t, z=t for t in [0, pi]
directional arrowhead on the helix around t ~ 2.2 pointing in the direction of increasing t
filled blue dot at the start point (1, 0, 0) with label '(1, 0, 0)'
filled blue dot at the end point (-1, 0, pi) with label '(-1, 0, pi)'
moving tracer dot on the helix driven by the t slider
on-screen readout showing current (x, y, z) = (cos t, sin t, t) and arc length s = sqrt(2)*t with increment ds = sqrt(2) dt

interactions.label: Parameter t
interactions.teaches: Sweeping t moves a point along the helix while the live readout shows (cos t, sin t, t) and the accumulated arc length s = sqrt(2)*t, making concrete that ds = sqrt((dx/dt)^2+(dy/dt)^2+(dz/dt)^2) dt = sqrt(2) dt is constant along this helix

Rotating the bounding box reveals how the single 3D helix projects to a circle in the xy-plane (top view) and to a sinusoid in the xz- and yz-planes (side views), explaining why x=cos t, y=sin t, z=t traces this path

demo_steps.title: Start of the path
demo_steps.narration: At t=0 the tracer sits at (1, 0, 0), the labeled start point at the bottom of the box. Arc length s = 0.

demo_steps.title: Halfway around
demo_steps.narration: At t = pi/2 the point is at (0, 1, pi/2): it has swung a quarter turn in xy while rising halfway in z. The readout shows s = sqrt(2)*(pi/2).

demo_steps.title: End of the path
demo_steps.narration: At t = pi the tracer reaches (-1, 0, pi), the labeled endpoint at the top. Total arc length is s = sqrt(2)*pi, the value used to set up the line integral.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World units map 1:1 to coordinates: box spans X in [-1,1] (width 2), Y in [-1,1] (depth 2), Z in [0, pi] (height ~3.1416). +X screen-right, +Y receding diagonal, +Z screen-up. Helix radius 1 in the xy-plane, z=t. Box edges thin dark lines #222222. Helix a thick tube/line in cyan-blue #2ba3d8. Start/end dots filled #2ba3d8 radius ~0.06. Arrowhead a small cone on the curve near t~2.2 oriented along the tangent (-sin t, cos t, 1). Parametric: x=cos t, y=sin t, z=t; speed |r'(t)| = sqrt(sin^2 t + cos^2 t + 1) = sqrt(2), so s(t)=sqrt(2)*t and ds=sqrt(2) dt. Axis tick labels: x at 1,0,-1; y at 1,-1; z at 0,pi. Use a standard isometric pose so all three box faces read as parallelograms (no true rectangle), matching the source.
interactionPlan.notes: Build the helix as a THREE.Line or TubeGeometry sampled at ~200 points over t in [0,pi]; reposition the tracer dot and refresh the HTML readout on every slider input. Keep the full curve always visible and let the tracer dot ride on top so orientation (arrowhead) stays clear. For orbit, enable OrbitControls with damping; no perspective foreshortening needed since axonometric pose is fixed by the renderer. Render tick labels and the (1,0,0)/(-1,0,pi) annotations as sprites or CSS2D labels so they remain legible while rotating.
